owner.occupation: Owner of a small ceramics and tableware shop in Alfama

world.bio: Dutch-born, in Lisbon for nine years. Used to design restaurant interiors in Rotterdam and Amsterdam; five years ago I opened Casa Prato, a small tableware shop on a steep street in Alfama. I sketch every plate, bowl and cup I plan to stock before I order it, which drives my suppliers a little mad. Customers are mostly restaurateurs, Airbnb hosts with taste, and people who walk in because of the blue door.
skills_assets: Casa Prato, 38 square metres in Alfama, plus an online shop shipping across the EU
Eleven years of restaurant interior and tableware specification experience
A sketchbook archive of roughly 400 plate and bowl designs
Relationships with eight restaurants in Lisbon and Porto that reorder tableware every season

projects.name: Winter collection 2026
projects.text: Six designs for the cold months: deep soup bowls, low plates, a lidded pot, two cup sizes. I want the glazes to look like wet stone and celadon, with the kiln marks left visible. I have the sketches in a folder, the colour cards pinned over my desk, and nobody to make them in the quantities I can sell. Launch target is early December, which is looking unlikely.

projects.name: Supplier replacement
projects.text: The Aveiro workshop that made my stoneware for four years closed in August when the owner retired. Spreadsheet of replacements has nine rows, four crossed out. One new factory replied but is asking for a 500-piece minimum per glaze. I sell maybe 60 of each design per season. The maths does not close.

projects.name: Alfama lease
projects.text: Landlord wants to turn the flat upstairs into a short-term rental and has hinted the shop's ceiling needs 'structural work'. Waiting for his letter.

notes.text: Portuguese lesson cancelled again by Teresa, third time this month. I am paying for a tutor I never see. Did the homework anyway, subjunctive of 'ter'. Ate pastel de nata out of spite.

Customer today, woman from Copenhagen, held a bowl for a full minute and asked who threw it. I said a factory. She put it back. Everyone wants to see a hand in it, a thumbprint. Why do I keep ordering perfect things?
The Aveiro workshop is really gone. Called Sr. Matos's number and his daughter answered, said he's growing tomatoes now. I am happy for him and I want to scream.
Factory number three wants 500 pieces per glaze. I did the sum on a napkin: at my pace that's eight seasons of one celadon bowl. No.
Long run along the Tagus, 8k, felt fine. Training for the October 10k. My knee clicks. Ana says I run like a heron.
Landlord stopped me on the stairs: 'Anouk, nothing personal.' Those are the worst words. He wants the flat upstairs for tourists and thinks the shop will 'adapt'.
Winter sketches all done. Six designs. The celadon bowl with the flat rim is the best thing I've drawn in years and it exists only as paper. Taped it above the till.
Customers keep asking for pieces that look hand-thrown, celadon-ish, kiln marks and all. Three people this week. One said she'd pay double for a bowl with a flame mark on it.
Accounts: the Aveiro gap already cost me about 4,000 euros in missed autumn restocks. Not catastrophic. Not good either.

messages.text: Ana: How's the shop? Anouk: Quiet, which is nice, and terrifying. Ana: And the supplier? Anouk: Dead. Ana: I'm sorry. Come for dinner, Francisco is making bacalhau.
Contact: Our minimum is 500 per glaze, per design. Anouk: I only need 50. Contact: Then I suggest a smaller supplier. Anouk: I know. Thank you for the honest answer.
Mum: You sound tired. Anouk: The shop is fine, the supplier closed. Mum: You could always come home and design restaurants. Anouk: Mum. Mum: I'm only saying.
Restaurateur: Do you have the grey-green bowls again? Anouk: Not until spring maybe. Restaurateur: We'll wait. Do the deep ones too.
Teresa: Desculpa, can we move to Thursday? Anouk: This is the fourth time. Teresa: I know, I'm sorry. Anouk: Next time I'm charging you.

calendar.event: Landlord meeting about the upstairs flat, 17:30

relations.about: Retired owner of the Aveiro workshop, now grows tomatoes; kind, a bit stubborn.
Best friend in Lisbon; bakery owner; tells me the truth.
Thinks I should move back to Holland and do interiors again.

constraints: Cannot hold inventory above about 6,000 euros at once
Will not stock anything mass-produced in Asia, a rule that is now costing her
Shop is closed Mondays, so no meetings that day
Needs lead time: winter pieces should be in by early December
sensitive: The shop's margin is thin; she has not paid herself a full salary since June
Worried that the lease problem could end the shop
Her sister is in debt and Anouk quietly sends 300 euros a month
